title: Polaris Cloud - Procurement: MSA/DPA, SLAs, Pricing & Onboarding
summary: Procurement and legal review for Redwood Inference. Discussed MSA and DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing bands for hosted vs dedicated, onboarding timeline, SOC2/KMS and data residency. Agreed to exchange redlines and pricing spreadsheet; pilot onboarding to begin after signature.

Schedule onboarding kickoff for week of 2026-03-23 once contracts signed

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Jared Kim (Polaris - Procurement); Aisha Rahman (Polaris - Legal); Diego Morales (Polaris - Head of Platform); Lena Park (Polaris - Security); Markus Varela (Polaris - FinOps)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - i'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Maya, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:14] Jared: Good thanks. busy week but we're ready to go. we've got procurement and legal on the line, so hoping to move the MSA/DPA forward.
[00:23] Aisha: Hi all. Aisha here, i'll be leading legal on our side. Diego and Lena are on for technical / security.
[00:30] Samir: Great. agenda for today - run through the MSA and DPA status, clarify any legal redlines, SLA expectations and credit mechanics, pricing questions (dedicated vs hosted), and agree next steps for onboarding.
[00:44] Maya: i'll also share a short note on what Dedicated entails - capacity, autoscaling, regions and what we can commit to.
[00:50] [00:50] Jared: sounds good. quick context: Polaris is evaluating vendors for inference across our document processing and chat assistants. security and data residency are hard blockers for certain workloads. we also need clear liability and termination terms for enterprise finance.
[01:08] Samir: understood. i'll call out the common things we see. two quick housekeeping things: 1) we are SOC 2 Type II, 2) we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and account-level KMS for Dedicated.
[01:23] Lena: when you say customer-managed KMS, do you mean HSM-level integration or just cloud KMS? we have strict encryption requirements and audit trails.
[01:31] Maya: good question - for Private we can integrate to your HSM/KMS via standard KMIP or cloud KMS; for Dedicated we can integrate to your cloud KMS and provide key wrapping so plaintext keys are not exposed in our control plane. audit logs are available via the console and can be pushed to your SIEM.
[01:50] Aisha: on the DPA i have two major items: data deletion obligations post-term; and a clause around data processing for improvement - you have some telemetry for model optimization, we want clarity that customer PII isn't used to train models.
[02:05] Samir: totally - our standard DPA prohibits using customer content to train models; we can add explicit language. for deletion, we support three options - immediate purge, 90-day retention for rollback (configurable), or specified archival if you request. which model do you need?
[02:20] Diego: immediate purge for most workloads, except for our analytics bucket where retention is fine but must be encrypted and reside in EU region.
[02:28] Maya: we can do region pinning on Dedicated and Private so the storage and logs stay in eu-west-1, and the control plane can be separated if needed.
[02:38] [02:38] Markus: let's talk SLAs - we need a 99.9% availability target for our customer-facing endpoints and a clear credit schedule. can Redwood commit to 99.9 for hosted? and what does Dedicated look like?
[02:52] Samir: hosted API standard SLA is 99.9; Dedicated offers a 99.95 SLA in paid tier with a higher commit. outages are measured at the route/endpoint level; credits are pro-rata and tiered. our legal team typically resists large liability caps but we have standard caps tied to fees paid in preceding 12 months - we can surface numbers in the MSA.
[03:15] Aisha: we will ask to adjust the liability cap for willful misconduct or gross negligence; also seeking indemnity carve-outs around data breaches and third-party claims.
[03:25] Samir: understood. we can review those clauses - some are negotiable, some are standard. i'll flag this to our legal ops and propose a redline response.
[03:32] [03:32] Jared: on pricing, Markus - you had some specific questions about Dedicated flat fees vs usage.
[03:36] Markus: yes. for Dedicated we need predictable monthly cost for a pool of GPUs. can we get a pricing sheet that lays out committed units, burst rates, and overage pricing? also how do token costs change if we use cached KV or quantized runtimes?
[03:50] Maya: yes, i'll share a spreadsheet - committed GPU pool cost + per-token variable for hosted fallback. with Dedicated, internal cost per token drops because KV caching and persistent state reduce repeated generation. quantized runtimes can cut GPU vram and cost, but there might be small quality delta; we can show tradeoffs.
[04:08] Diego: is there a cost for private deployment licensing? we expect a platform license + support fee.
[04:13] Samir: Private has a base platform fee plus services for on-prem install and support. we'll include that in the pricing sheet.
[04:20] [04:20] Aisha: back to the MSA - termination for convenience: we want 30 days notice for non-critical contracts. your MSA lists 90 days. can that be shortened; and what about transition assistance terms?
[04:34] Samir: our standard is 90 days for enterprise deals, but for strategic customers we can negotiate 30-60; transition assistance is standard two-week support and data export assistance - can add extended transition assistance as a billable service.
[04:48] Jared: we also need clear onboarding milestones tied to payment triggers: signature -> provisioning -> pilot -> production. can we map those?
[04:57] Maya: yes - typical flow: sign -> provisioning (2 weeks) -> pilot (4 weeks) -> production roll. provisioning times vary by region and model sizes. we'll propose a schedule in the onboarding doc.
[05:12] [05:12] Lena: for audit logs and SSO - we need SAML 2.0 integration, RBAC mapping to AD groups, and 1 year of log retention in our SIEM. is that supported?
[05:23] Maya: SAML 2.0 is supported, RBAC can map to AD groups, and logs can be exported via syslog or pushed to your cloud logging via a secure forwarder. retention length is customer-side, we can keep exports as long as you want in your storage.
[05:38] Aisha: DPA also requires subprocessor list. can you provide an exhaustive list and current SOC2 scope?
[05:45] Samir: yes - we'll attach a subprocessor list and our SOC 2 attestation. currently SOC 2 Type II scope includes platform, infra, and support. subprocessors include major cloud providers and monitoring vendors - we'll provide an up-to-date list.
[05:59] [05:59] Jared: one item - our procurement head wants an acceptance criteria for pilot success (latency p95 under X ms, throughput Y qps). how do you instrument that?
[06:08] Maya: we generate token-level latency metrics and can provide dashboards per route and model, p50/p95/p99, and custom traces. for pilots we can run benchmarks with your datasets and produce a perf baseline report.
[06:22] Diego: will Redwood run benchmarks in our environment or in Redwood infra? prefer in our VPC to test network egress and region.
[06:29] Maya: for Private and Dedicated we can run in your VPC; for hosted we can do controlled mimic tests. we'll need sample payloads and acceptance STL.
[06:41] [06:41] Markus: on pricing approvals, procurement needs a 3-tier quote: pilot rate, committed Dedicated rate, and enterprise volume discount. also what payment terms - net30? net45?
[06:51] Samir: standard is net30; for enterprise we can do net45 with pre-approved credit terms. we'll provide three quote lines.
[06:59] Aisha: any compliance items specific to EU? data residency and Schrems II considerations - we need explicit routing and not to transfer EU PII to US without safeguards.
[07:10] Maya: we have region pinning and can keep data in eu-west-1; for control plane escrow we can discuss a separate agreement. we can also sign an EU data processing addendum with SCCs or equivalent.
[07:23] [07:23] Samir: i'll note that as a legal item; also on model outputs - if you need redaction or PII scrubbing we have pre/post-processing hooks and can include that in the integration plan.
[07:34] Diego: curious about log access - can Polaris have direct read-only access to the logs, or are you pushing them?
[07:41] Maya: read-only access to our console is an option for some tiers; otherwise we push logs to your logging endpoint. for Dedicated you can have an instance of the console inside your VPC with direct access.
[07:54] [07:54] Jared: ok, let's surface the top legal redlines from our side now. Aisha?
[07:58] Aisha: top five: 1) Lower liability cap for data breaches; 2) Warranty around data handling and no-training clause explicitly in the DPA; 3) 30 day termination for convenience; 4) Clear SLA credit schedule and remedy; 5) Audit rights or SOC2 audits available on request.
[08:18] Samir: all reasonable. we'll prepare a redline response, and where policy prevents us from changing a standard clause we'll flag with rationale.
[08:26] [08:26] Diego: on technical lead time - if we sign, how quickly can we get Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 for the pilot?
[08:33] Maya: typical provisioning is 1-2 weeks for Dedicated in common regions; if it's a high-memory model or larger GPU we may need additional lead time. we'll include expected timelines in the onboarding doc.
[08:46] Markus: what about penalties for missing critical deadlines during onboarding? sometimes we need hard commitments.
[08:52] Samir: we can include onboarding milestones and remedy options (credits or staff escalation). we'll propose a mutual SLA for onboarding in the statement of work.
[09:03] [09:03] Jared: let me ask procurement question - do you accept our standard redlines template or do we have to follow your MSA format?
[09:11] Aisha: typically vendors will take our redline doc and mark changes.
[09:14] Samir: we'll accept your redline and return a clean redline set with comments. prefer to stick to Redwood MSA structure for clarity but we'll be flexible.
[09:22] [09:22] Maya: quick note on telemetry: we can offer an option to scrub PII before it leaves customer boundary - it's part of the integration configuration.
[09:30] Diego: that's important for some of our use cases.
[09:33] [09:33] Jared: procurement would also like to know the SLA credit math upfront - if 99.9 is missed, what percent credit do we get?
[09:40] Samir: standard is 5% of monthly invoice for <99.9 but >=99.0, and incremental higher credits for larger breaches. we'll share the exact table.
[09:50] Aisha: can we get a defined escalation path for security incidents and breach notification timings? 72 hours for initial notice is in our policy.
[09:58] Maya: yes, our incident playbook includes initial notification within 72 hours, and full report within 30 days. we have an on-call security contact.
[10:09] [10:09] Jared: let's anchor dates - Samir, you'll send an MSA + DPA clean set by 2026-03-09; Maya you'll share pricing and dedicated perf baseline by 2026-03-07. Polaris will return redlines by 2026-03-16. Pilot start contingent on signatures week of 2026-03-23. does that work?
[10:26] Samir: yes. we'll also include subprocessors and SOC2 in the attachments.
[10:30] Markus: last thing - any start-of-service credits or pilot discounts?
[10:33] Samir: we typically offer a pilot discount on hosted usage credits; for Dedicated we can offer a short-term pilot rate for the first month. i'll include numbers in the pricing sheet.
[10:44] Aisha: good. also, we'll request that indemnity and liability cap language be highlighted in your redline so our legal can focus.
[10:50] Samir: will do.
[10:53] [10:53] Diego: one minor transcription note - some product names got swapped in earlier emails, please confirm the model variants we plan to use (redwood-curie-v1 etc) so we have consistent naming.
[11:03] Maya: i'll include a model mapping table in the onboarding doc - model alias to actual model artifact and perf characteristics.
[11:11] [11:11] Jared: ok folks, that covers main items. appreciate the clarity. any final questions?
[11:15] Aisha: none from legal.
[11:17] Markus: just to reconfirm payment terms - you will provide net30 and alternative net45 for enterprise, and we'll pick during PO stage.
[11:24] Samir: correct.
[11:26] [11:26] Samir: recap of next steps: Samir send MSA/DPA and subprocessors + SOC2 by 2026-03-09; Maya send pricing sheet and perf baseline by 2026-03-07; Polaris to return redlines and pilot acceptance criteria by 2026-03-16; schedule onboarding if contract signed for week of 2026-03-23.
[11:46] Jared: great, thanks everyone. we'll watch for docs and get legal engaged.
[11:50] Samir: thanks all - we'll follow up in email with attachments. bye.

End of transcript. Note: transcript contains occasional mishearings and generic speaker labels where Fireflies auto-attributed; timestamps are approximate.
